title: Netherlands – Repair and maintenance services of electrical and mechanical building installations – Beheer, onderhoud en projecten voor de vastgoedportefeuilles werkplaatsen, kantoren en dienstverblijven.
description: De opdracht betreft integrale hardservice-dienstverlening voor de vastgoedportefeuilles van Concern Huisvesting. De opdracht heeft betrekking op Werkplaatsen, Magazijnen en Terreinen en, vanaf 1 juni 2028, kantoren en dienstverblijven. Binnen de opdracht worden per perceel drie samenhangende onderdelen onderscheiden: uitvoeringswerkzaamheden, advieswerkzaamheden en technisch locatiemanagement. Deze onderdelen vormen gezamenlijk één dienstverlening. De hardservicepartner moet in staat zijn operationele werkzaamheden te verbinden met tactische advisering en de strategische doelstellingen van NS en Concern Huisvesting. De uitvoeringswerkzaamheden omvatten preventief onderhoud, correctief onderhoud inclusief een 24/7/365-storingsdienst, planmatig en vervangingsonderhoud, mutaties en modificaties, verduurzamingsprojecten en huisvestingsprojecten. De integrale hardservice-dienstverlening heeft betrekking op de disciplines werktuigbouwkunde, elektrotechniek, bouwkunde, transportinstallaties, terreinen en safety en security. De opdracht is verdeeld in twee geografische percelen: Perceel Noord en Perceel Zuid. Gegadigden kunnen zich aanmelden voor Perceel Noord, Perceel Zuid of voor beide percelen. Aan één inschrijver wordt uiteindelijk maximaal één perceel gegund. Per perceel wordt één raamovereenkomst gesloten met één leverancier voor een periode van 72 maanden, met de mogelijkheid de raamovereenkomst tweemaal met 12 maanden te verlengen.

title: Germany – Staff training services – Ausschreibung Führungskräfteentwicklung (FKE)
description: Die DFS Deutsche Flugsicherung GmbH (nachstehend DFS genannt) schreibt Rahmenvereinbarungen zur Durchführung von Führungskräftetrainings aus. Wir sichern die Zukunftsfähigkeit des DFS-Konzerns, indem wir Führungskräfte bedarfsgerecht und zukunftsorientiert weiterentwickeln und so langfristig an uns binden. Die Führungskräfte sollen befähigt werden, ihr volles Potenzial auszuschöpfen und ihre Mitarbeitenden langfristig motivieren, es ihnen gleich zu tun. Im Rahmen des Führungsalltags entsteht für Führungskräfte der Bedarf, zu Aspekten der Selbstführung, Leadership, Management und Change Management gezielt Wissen zu erwerben und vertiefen. Ebenso sollen Führungskräfte bei der Übernahme einer Führungsposition und in der persönlichen Weiterentwicklung durch Erstauseinandersetzung mit dem Thema Führung im Rahmen eines Führungscampus mit verschiedenen Modulen unterstützt werden. Ergänzt werden können die verschiedenen Formate noch um Refresher oder Erfahrungskreise für eine gezielte Reflexion der eigenen Entwicklung der Führungskräfte nach dem Training. Es handelt sich hierbei um eine moderierte Austauschplattform (Präsenz oder virtuell) für die Trainingsteilnehmenden, bei dem sich die Führungskräfte unter Verwendung verschiedener Methoden zu Fragen oder Erfahrungswerten austauschen können. Dabei können konkrete Fragestellungen aus dem eigenen Arbeitsalltag oder DFS-aktuelle Themen bearbeitet werden. Der Auftrag wird in 3 Losen vergeben: Los 1: Führungscampus mit 5 Modulen Los 2: Führungskräftetrainings zu Führung & Kommunikation Los 3: Lernreise Leading Change Bei Los 1 „Führungscampus“ sollen die Module ca. zwei- bis dreimal jährlich in Präsenz am Standort Langen stattfinden. Ergänzt werden können die Module durch virtuelle Elemente sowie Theorie-Input mit Learning Nuggets. Die Häufigkeit der Veranstaltungen variiert je nach Bedarf. Bei Los 2 „Führungskräftetrainings“ und Los 3 „Leading Change“ sollen die Trainings zwei- bis fünfmal jährlich primär in Präsenz am Standort Langen, gegebenenfalls auch an anderen Orten in Deutschland oder auch virtuell, stattfinden. Die Häufigkeit der Veranstaltungen variiert je nach Bedarf. Die Durchführung der vorgenannten Veranstaltungen beinhaltet in der Regel: - die Vorbereitung (Konzeption) - die Durchführung (Moderation) - die Nachbereitung sowie - die Bereitstellung von lehrgangsbegleitendem Material für jeden Trainings-Teilnehmenden Die DFS behält sich vor, für die verschiedenen Lose unterschiedlich viele Kooperations-Partner auszuwählen.

title: Maintenance Services for Rohde & Schwarz Equipment
description: 1. Description of Requirement: The First Responder Network Authority intends to award a firm-fixed-price, sole source purchase order to Rohde & Schwarz USA, Inc. (R&S) for maintenance, repair, and calibration services on the following Government-owned R&S equipment. 2. Authority: Competition is limited to a single source in accordance with [insert correct authority RFO FAR 6.103-1. 3. Basis for Sole Source Determination: Market research confirms that the subject system is proprietary to R&S. R&S is the original equipment manufacturer (OEM) and the only authorized repair and calibration facility in North America for R&S products. Because R&S controls the design, genuine replacement parts, and calibration standards for this equipment, only the OEM can restore the system to original specifications, maintain system compatibility, and preserve existing warranty coverage. Obtaining these services from any other source would risk degraded performance, loss of warranty protection, and disruption of equipment operability. 4. Nature of This Notice: This Notice of Intent is not a request for competitive quotes, and no solicitation documents exist for this requirement. Telephone or email requests for a solicitation will not be honored. 5. Instructions to Interested Sources: Any responsible source that believes it can meet this requirement must submit a capability statement by the response due date identified above. The capability statement must provide management and technical data in sufficient detail, with convincing evidence, to clearly demonstrate the source's capability to perform the required services, including evidence of OEM authorization to repair and calibrate the identified equipment. Submissions limited to requests for documentation or additional information, or to questions alone, will not be considered. Capability statements must be submitted by email to the point of contact listed above and may not exceed 2 pages. 6. Government Reservation of Rights: Responses to this notice are for informational and planning purposes only and will not be considered offers. The Government will not pay for any information submitted. All capability statements received by the due date will be evaluated solely to determine whether to conduct a competitive procurement or proceed with a sole source purchase order. The determination of whether to compete this requirement is solely within the discretion of the Government. If no responses are received, or if no response demonstrates the capability to meet the requirement, the Contracting Officer will proceed with a sole source award to R&S. Responses are due by 8:00AM (EST), 11 November 2026 to Brandon Payne, Contracting Officer; brandon.payne@firstnet.gov.

Tilaajana hankinnassa on Mäntsälän kunta, Kiinteistö Oy Mäntsälän Toimistotalo, sekä Mäntsälän Sotekiinteistöt Oy. Puitesopimuksen kesto on kaksi (2) vuotta 1.1.2027 - 31.12.2028. Hankinta sisältää kaksi yhden (1+1) vuoden optiota kausille 1.1.-31.12.2029 ja 1.1.-31.12.2030. Hankintaa on jaettu kahteen osakokonaisuuteen, tarjouksen voi jättää yhteen tai useampaan osaan. Tarjouskilpailun tavoitteena on valita osakokonaisuuteen: 1. Rakennusautomaatiotyöt / Deos- järjestelmät, kolme (3) kokonaistaloudellisesti edullisinta ja vähimmäisvaatimukset täyttävää toimittajaa. 2. Rakennusautomaatiotyöt / Struxture- järjestelmät, kolme (3) kokonaistaloudellisesti edullisinta ja vähimmäisvaatimukset täyttävää toimittajaa. Jos tarjouksia ei saada riittävästi tai tarjouksia joudutaan hylkäämään, voi valittavien toimittajien määrä osa-alueittain olla vähemmän. Valittujen toimittajien kanssa perustetaan puitejärjestely. Tarjouspyyntö koskee seuraavia rakennusautomaatioon liittyviä töitä: Rakennusautomaation huolto- ja ylläpitotyöt Rakennusautomaation vikakorjaukset Rakennusautomaatioon liittyvät pienet muutostyöt Rakennusautomaatiourakat kiinteällä kokonaishinnalla Rakennusautomaatiotyöt tuntiveloituksella Rakennusautomaatiojärjestelmän käyttötyöt Mäntsälän kunnalla on pääosin käytössä Struxure Ware- ja Deos-järjestelmät, tämän vuoksi urakoitsijalla pitää olla mahdollisuus tarjoamansa osakokonaisuuden järjestelmän ylläpitoon, ohjelmointiin ja huoltoon. Tämän vuoksi tarjoajalla pitää olla sopimuskumppanuus, partner- tai vastaava järjestely kyseisen/kyseisten automaatiojärjestelmien toimittajien kanssa, joka oikeuttaa järjestelmien asennuksen, ylläpidon ja muutostyöt. Hankintasopimuksen perusteella tilaaja tekee toimittajilta tilauksia, joiden kesto ja mahdolliset tilausta koskevat yksityiskohdat määräytyvät tilaajan tarpeiden mukaan. Tarjouspyyntö koskee tilaajan kiinteistöjä ja toimitiloja sekä niissä sopimusaikana toteutettavia erikseen määriteltäviä työsuorituksia/kokonaisuuksia. Kunnossapitotöiden lisäksi sopimuksen kautta tilataan vuosittaisia investointitöitä. Töiden kesto tapauskohtaisesti noin yhdestä (1) tunnista muutamaan kuukauteen. Työt tilataan laskutustyönä tuntiveloitusperiaatteella tai erikseen puitesopimustoimittajien kesken kilpailutettavalla urakkahinnalla. Työt tehdään YSE 1998 rakennusurakan yleisten sopimusehtojen sekä hankekohtaisten urakka-asiakirjojen mukaisesti. Mikäli yksittäisen toimeksiannon ennakoitu arvo ylittää 50 000 euroa (alv 0 %), tilaajalla on oikeus edellyttää urakoitsijalta rakennusajan vakuus ja takuuajan vakuus. Vakuuden määrä YSE98 mukaisesti ellei sopimuksessa toisin sovita. Vakuuden tulee olla pankki-, vakuutus- tai muu tilaajan hyväksymä omavelkainen takaus., Rakennusautomaatiotyöt / Deos-järjestelmät Puitesopimuksen perusteella tehtävät työt voivat käsittää rakennusautomaatiojärjestelmien huolto-, vianhaku-, korjaus-, muutos-, ohjelmointi-, saneeraus-, käyttöönotto- ja optimointitöitä. Töihin sisältyvät tarpeen mukaan VAK- ja alakeskustyöt, kenttälaitteiden asennukset ja uusimiset, aikaohjelmien, asetusarvojen, säätöpiirien, ohjausten ja hälytysten muutokset sekä mittaus-, ohjaus-, indikointi- ja hälytyspisteiden lisääminen ja muuttaminen. Työt voivat sisältää myös LVI- ja sähköjärjestelmien liittämistä rakennusautomaatioon, valvomografiikoiden laatimista ja päivittämistä sekä järjestelmien välisten tiedonsiirtoyhteyksien ja integraatioiden toteuttamista. title: Finland – Construction work – Kaivokselan koulu korjaus ja tilamuutokset
description: Hankinta käsittää Kaivokselan koulun perusparannus –hankkeen rakennusurakan / pääurakan työt urakkalaskenta-asiakirjojen mukaisesti. Työt tehdään tilaajan laadituttamien suunnitelmien mukaan. Rakennusurakoitsija toimii pääurakoitsijana. Tilaaja hankkii pääurakkaan alistettavina sivu-urakoina: putki-, ilmanvaihto-, sähkö- ja rakennusautomaatiourakat. Rakennusurakoitsija toimii myös urakan ajan kohteen päätoteuttajana sekä työmaan johtovelvollisuuksista ja työmaapalveluista vastaavana urakoitsijana. Urakkakilpailu toteutetaan avoimella menettelyllä. Tilaaja on tarjouspyynnössä määrittänyt tarjoajalta vaadittavat kelpoisuus- /soveltuvuusehdot. title: Finland – Gas compressors – Reciprocating compressor packages for natural gas compression service
description: Gasgrid Finland Oy (hereinafter “Contracting Authority”) is a state-owned gas transmission system operator (TSO) that started operating in early 2020. The company mission is to ensure cost-effective, safe and undisturbed gas transmission and to actively develop the gas market and the Finnish energy system. The company has the overall system responsibility for the entire methane gas transmission network in Finland. The Contracting Authority is planning to construct a natural gas compression station to Lempäälä, Finland. Construction work is scheduled to be started approx. Q2/2027. Installation of the compressor unit(s) is planned to be started approx. Q2/2028. The schedule mentioned is indicative and subject to changes. In this procurement the Contracting Authority is looking for a supplier for 2+1 (option) complete, electrically driven API 618 reciprocating compressor packages for natural gas compression service to Gasgrid’s Lempäälä gas compression station. The key specifications as follows (but not limited to these): - Each compressor package shall comprise one electrically driven API 618 reciprocating compressor unit, together with the associated process equipment, auxiliaries, electrical equipment, instrumentation, control and safety systems, and other equipment necessary to provide a complete, safe and operable compressor package suitable for integration into the Compressor Station. - The Supplier shall be responsible for the design, manufacture, testing, documentation, delivery, integration and conformity of the complete compressor package within the final agreed scope of supply. The Supplier shall also be responsible for defining and managing the necessary technical and safety interfaces between the compressor package and systems or equipment supplied by the Contracting Authority, EPCM Contractor or other parties, to the extent necessary for the safe integration and conformity of the compressor package. - The anticipated operating envelope of each compressor unit is approximately 3,000 Nm³/h, with suction pressure approximately 4–8 barg and discharge pressure up to approximately 54 barg. -The compressor packages shall comply with all applicable European Union and Finnish legislation and requirements, including the applicable requirements of the Machinery Regulation (EU) 2023/1230 Annex V, Part A – Declaration of Conformity for Completed Machinery, PED 2014/68/EU, ATEX 2014/34/EU and EMC 2014/30/EU. -The Supplier shall be capable of fulfilling the applicable manufacturer obligations and conformity assessment requirements for the complete compressor package, including provision of the required declarations, CE marking and conformity documentation. Site supervision and commissioning support, including support for the required on-site conformity and CE marking activities, are included. Installation at site is excluded from the scope of supply. Detailed technical requirements, operating conditions, performance requirements, scope boundaries, interfaces and documentation requirements will be defined in the procurement documentation issued during the subsequent phase of the procurement procedure.

title: Notice of Intent to solicit a single source � Fish and Macroinvertebrate (Nekton) Monitoring (St. Johns River)
description: NOTICE OF INTENT TO SOLICIT A SINGLE SOURCE The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers (USACE), Jacksonville District intends to solicit and contract with Fish & Wildlife Research Institute (CAGE 3UWN3), of St. Petersburg, FL, on a sole-source basis, RFO 6.103-1(b), to conduct Nekton monitoring within selected zones of the Lower St. Johns River (LSJR) as well as selected tributaries in Northeast Florida. The Florida Fish and Wildlife Conservation Commission (FWC) Fish and Wildlife Research Institute�s (FWRI) Fisheries-Independent Monitoring (FIM) program is a long-term program designed to monitor the relative abundance of fishery resources in Florida�s major estuarine, coastal, and reef systems. FWRI works for the State of Florida. The applicable North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code assigned to this procurement is 541620, Environmental Consulting Services. The USACE, in cooperation with the Jacksonville Port Authority (JaxPort), conducted a comprehensive economic, engineering, and environmental study to examine the effects of increasing the depth of the existing Federally maintained channel in the LSJR from the current depth of 40-feet to a maximum depth of 47-feet between the mouth, at Mayport Florida, and river mile 13. Construction of the deepening was completed in 2022. Channel deepening allows for the access of larger vessels (Panamax and New Panamax classes) to deliver cargo to existing JaxPort terminals around Blount Island. As part of this evaluation, computer modeling scenarios have been completed on the potential effects that the channel deepening might have on water quality, circulation patterns, salinity gradients, and a variety of ecological components (wetland vegetation, SAV, benthos, plankton, and nekton) in the LSJR. Over 100 nekton species have been documented as using the estuarine portion of the LSJR and many of these species represent important commercial and recreational fisheries (i.e., Blue Crab, White Shrimp, and Red Drum). Two specific areas in need of consideration with respect to nekton are: 1) potential effects of salinity changes on the spawning success, recruitment, and population dynamics of important recreational, commercial, and forage nekton and, 2) potential effects of salinity changes on critical nekton habitat within the LSJR estuary. Within the estuary, channel deepening has the potential to affect salinity and water quality gradients, most likely by shifting distributions in these gradients within the estuary. These shifts may affect spawning and nursery habitats and ultimately influence reproductive and recruitment success of estuarine-dependent nekton. Of particular concern, are the tributaries and coves located between river kilometers (km) 14 and 48 and the estuarine portion upstream of Julington Creek (river km 64 � 134). These tributaries between river kilometers 14 and 48 (Trout, Arlington, and Ortega rivers) and the estuarine section upstream of Julington Creek are highly influenced by freshwater inflow and generally have lower salinities than other portions of the LSJR estuary. The freshwater influence provides low salinity habitats that many estuarine and marine nekton require during their early life history stages. Previously collected data suggests that many recreationally and commercially important estuarine-dependent species (i.e. members of the Sciaenidae family [drums], White Shrimp, Blue Crab, and mullet) utilize these habitats during different times of the year and that these areas likely represent critical habitats for maintaining healthy stocks of these species in the LSJR estuary and adjacent coastal waters. Also, of concern with regards to potential changes in salinity would be impacts on resident freshwater species, especially within the Trout, Arlington, and Ortega rivers. Salinity increases could decrease the availability of freshwater habitat, thereby reducing the abundance of freshwater species in these tidal tributaries. The salinity and fish modeling done by the USACE predicted some minor changes in the distributions of some species. The most recognizable pattern was the predicted shift of some moderate to low salinity habitats upstream in the lower St. Johns River. Predicted changes in Mill Cove salinity also may result in some habitat loss for young-of-the-year and juvenile life history stages for a few species. Young-of-the-year and juveniles from numerous nekton species utilize this habitat during ingress, egress, and as nursery habitats. A better understanding of the relationships between channel deepening, salinity, water quality, water flow, estuarine habitats, and the abundance of estuarine-dependent and freshwater-resident nekton species that inhabit these portions of the LSJR estuary is necessary to gauge the effects that channel deepening has on this estuary. The long-term sampling proposed here would increase the resolution of nekton data within select tidal tributaries and coves and would continue the long-term sampling upstream of Julington Creek. These data will allow for the assessment of the effects of channel deepening on nekton assemblages in these critical LSJR estuarine habitats. Based on the foregoing, Florida Fish and Wildlife Conservation Commission is determined to be the only responsible source. No solicitation will be posted for this requirement. No telephone requests will be honored. If you have any questions concerning this opportunity, please contact: Ms. Florutha A Robinson, Contract Specialist, at florutha.a.robinson@usace.army.mil or Mr. Gary R Weir, Contracting Officer, at gary.r.weir@usace.army.mil. Any potential source may contact the persons indicated above to discuss their ability to offer the required services for future acquisitions.

description: Waterways Ireland stocks a selection of printed literature and publications at a central storage location from where the products are then distributed to individual or business customers upon instruction from Waterways Ireland or upon order generated directly from the Waterways Ireland web shop via email. The Organisation uses the distribution centre for direct mail, pick, pack and postage, as well as the storage of quantities of literature and smart cards. Waterways Ireland now seeks the services of a supplier to continue this distribution of products through a streamlined logistics system involving the fulfilment of web shop orders and distribution to customers through appropriate ‘pick, pack and postage’ and bulk distribution mechanisms. Transparent stock control and reporting are essential.

description: Stichting IMN past de Europese openbare aanbestedingsprocedure toe conform de Aanbestedingswet 2012. In 117 rayons is eerder dit jaar door een onderhandelingsprocedure een Bergingsovereenkomst 2026 - 2031 tot stand gekomen. De nu voorliggende aanbesteding heeft betrekking op de 99 rayons waarin nog geen bergingsovereenkomst werd gesloten. De rayons waar het om gaat zijn opgesomd in de Rayonlijst 2027 - 2031 (zie 1.3 Aanbestedingsleidraad). Onderwerp van aanbesteding is de Bergingsovereenkomst 2027 - 2031. Deze is, afgezien van de looptijd, identiek aan de in 117 rayons al tot stand gekomen Bergingsovereenkomst 2026 - 2031. Ieder aan te besteden rayon geldt als een zelfstandige opdracht en is onderwerp van een zelfstandige aanbestedingsprocedure. De gunningsbeslissingen in elk rayon zijn onafhankelijk van elkaar behoudens het gestelde in paragraaf 7.3. Dit betekent dat Stichting IMN voor ieder rayon kan besluiten om, als de omstandigheden daarnaar zijn, de aanbesteding in te trekken. De aanbesteding heeft uitsluitend betrekking op de in de Rayonlijst 2027 - 2031 vermelde rayons. (https://www.stichtingimn.nl/rayons.php). De nu voorliggende aanbesteding heeft betrekking op de 99 rayons.

title: H399--Elevator Inspection Service FHCC VAMC in North Chicago IL Base 4 OY
description: SOURCES SOUGHT SYNOPSIS The Department of Veterans Affairs is issuing this sources sought synopsis as a means of conducting market research to identify parties having an interest in and the resources to support a requirement for Elevator Testing Services located at FHCC VAMC , North Chicago IL. o Captain James A. Lovell Federal Health Care Center, North Chicago, IL. The result of this market research will contribute to determining the method of procurement. The applicable North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code assigned to this procurement is 341350. THERE IS NO SOLICITATION AT THIS TIME. This request for capability information does not constitute a request for proposals; submission of any information in response to this market survey is purely voluntary; the government assumes no financial responsibility for any costs incurred. Background: The purpose of this Contract is to provide for the inspection/testing of the vertical transportation system located at the Captain James A. Lovell Federal Health Care Center ( FHCC ), 3001 Green Bay Road, North Chicago, IL 60064-3048, as set forth in this Performance Work Statement. A complete listing of all vertical transportation system components, including thirty-one (31) elevators, two (2) cart lifts, and two (2) dumbwaiters (collectively VTS components ), is set forth in the Vertical Transportation System Schedule at the end of this Performance Work Statement. Any additional vertical transportation system components put into service after award of this Contract shall be included in the Vertical Transportation System Schedule at price(s) consistent with the current Price Schedule. A complete listing of all VTS Components, including twenty-nine (31) elevators, two (2) cart lifts, and two (2) dumbwaiters, is set forth in the Vertical Transportation System Schedule at the end of this Statement of Work. Any additional vertical transportation system components put into service after award of this Contract shall be included in the Vertical Transportation System Inventory at price(s) consistent with the current Price Schedule. If your organization has the potential capacity to perform these contract services, please provide the following information: 1) Organization name, address, email address, website address, if applicable, telephone number, and size and type of ownership for the organization; and 2) Tailored capability statements addressing the particulars of this effort and documentation supporting claims of organizational and staff capability. If significant subcontracting or teaming is anticipated in order to deliver technical capability, organizations should address the administrative and management structure of such arrangements. The Government will evaluate market information to ascertain potential market capacity to provide services consistent in scope and scale with those described in this notice and otherwise anticipated. BASED ON THE RESPONSES TO THIS SOURCES SOUGHT NOTICE/MARKET RESEARCH, THIS REQUIREMENT MAY BE SET-ASIDE FOR SDVOSB. Telephone inquiries will not be accepted or acknowledged, and no feedback or evaluations will be provided to companies regarding their submissions. Submission Instructions: Interested parties who consider themselves qualified to perform the above-listed services are invited to submit a response to this Sources Sought Notice by 10:00AM Local Time (Central) on November 11th, 2026. All responses under this Sources Sought Notice shall be emailed to Michelle.Klug2@va.gov. STATEMENT OF WORK Inspections Overview: The Contractor shall perform Annual Category 1, Semiannual, and Full-Load Category 5 VTS component inspection/testing as follows: a. Annual Category 1 inspection/testing is typically conducted in May of each year; a. Semiannual inspection/testing is typically conducted in November of each year; and b. Full-Load Category 5 testing will be performed in November 2027. c. Note: Typical inspection/testing dates are subject to change, in FHCC s sole discretion. Basic Contractor Responsibilities: The Contractor shall provide all personnel, equipment, material, parts, software, supplies, facilities, transportation, tools, materials, supervision, and other items and non-personal services necessary for execution of the work to be performed under this Contract. Any work found to be non-conforming to the terms of this Contract shall be promptly corrected by the Contractor at no additional cost to the Government. All work shall be performed in a neat and professional manner, including the removal of all trash and debris at the completion of all work. Contractor Limitations: The Contractor performing inspection/testing under this Contract is prohibited from performing any repairs or other work on any of the VTS components covered by this Contract. Safety: All work performed under this Contract shall conform to such safety precautions as the FHCC Fire/Safety and Engineering Departments determine, in their sole discretion, to be necessary, in addition to all other requirements set forth elsewhere in the Contract. Inspection/Testing Standards. 1. All inspection/testing of FHCC s vertical transportation system components shall comply with the most current version of the following standards: a. American Society of Mechanical Engineers ( ASME ) 17.1: Handbook on Safety Code for Elevators and Escalators; b. ASME 17.2: Guide for Inspection of Elevators, Escalators, and Moving Walks; c. ASME 17.3: Safety Code for Existing Elevators and Escalators; d. National Fire Protection Association ( NFPA ) 70: National Electrical Code; and e. NFPA 70E: Standard for Electrical Safety in the Workplace. 2. During any inspection/testing, parts shall be removed and equipment cleaned, as necessary, to determine their exact condition. All parts shall be properly reinstalled after removal. 3. All inspections shall be performed in the presence of an elevator maintenance technician, currently under contract as the VA elevator maintenance contractor, and the COR or designated FHCC representative. 4. Immediately following the conclusion of each inspection/testing, the Contractor shall brief the COR or designated FHCC representative regarding the inspection/testing results, including without limitation: code violations, safety concerns, and immediate maintenance needs. 5. The COR, in the COR s sole discretion, may reject any work performed under this Contract that is noncompliant with any of the requirements set forth in this Contract. All rejected work shall be corrected as quickly as reasonably possible at no additional expense to the Government. Inspection Checklists: The Contractor shall provide a fully completed inspection checklist applicable to each VTS component using the Checklist for Inspection of Electric Elevators The comments section of each checklist shall include a. If the VTS component is safe operating condition; a. If the VTS component will perform in accordance with Original Equipment Manufacturer ( OEM ) standards; b. Whether the VTS component has been altered, except in conformity with all applicable standards set forth in this Contract; c. If the VTS component has any deficiencies, referencing the appropriate standard as applicable; and d. Whether there are any recommended VTS component repairs or upgrades. e. Documentation. Upon completion of the inspection/testing of all FHCC s VTS components, the Contractor shall provide a report within thirty (30) days to the COR and other FHCC personnel as directed. The report shall be electronically submitted in pdf format utilizing word processing to the maximum extent practicable; individual file size shall not exceed 7 MB. Each report should include: Certificates of Inspection: The Certificate of Inspection for each VTS component shall include the following information: a. Location (building and city/state); a. Identification number; b. Capacity; c. Speed; d. Date of inspection; e. Name of inspector and company; f. Inspector s sign

title: Germany – Underground work other than tunnels, shafts and subways – BBA, Neubau Halle 4 Neubau VE206 Tiefbauarbeiten - Baugrubenherstellung
description: Die Hamburger Hochbahn AG beabsichtigt die Vergabe der Leistungen für die Errichtung einer Baugrube für den Neubau einer U-Bahn-Werkstatthalle in Hamburg-Barmbek. Auf dem U Bahn Betriebshof Barmbek wird eine vorhandene Werkstatthalle (Halle 4) für U-Bahn-Betriebs- und Fahrgastfahrzeuge abgerissen und im Anschluss neu errichtet. Das Grundstück ist zwischen den Bahngleisen der U-Bahnlinie 3, den Bahngleisen der S-Bahnlinie 1, dem Barmbeker Stichkanal und der Hellbrookstraße gelegen. Das Baufeld befindet sich an der südlichen Grundstücksgrenzen entlang der Bahngleise der U Bahnlinie U3. Die Zufahrt zu dem Baufeld ist nur von der Hellbrookstraße aus entlang der Nord-Süd-Achse des Grundstücks möglich. Alle weiteren Gebäude und Anlagen auf dem Hof inkl. der Gleisharfe sind während der gesamten Baumaßnahme weiterhin in Betrieb. Flächen für die Baustelleneinrichtung stehen nur begrenzt zur Verfügung. Die Bestandshalle aus den 1910-er Jahren wird im Vorfeld auf einer Fläche von rd. 4.300 m² bis auf Geländeebene rückgebaut. Das Kellergeschoss bleibt bestehen und wird mit Abbruchmaterial verfüllt. Der Rückbau des Kellers erfolgt mit Aushub der Baugrube. Der Neubau umfasst eine vollflächig unterkellerte Werkstatthalle mit einer Grundfläche von rd. 5.700 m² sowie zwei aufgehenden Geschossen, die bereichsweise über der Hallendecke errichtet und für Nebenwerkstätten und Ausbildungszwecke genutzt werden
